title: Final Exit Visa Saudi Arabia: Processing Times & New Rules
description: How many days to process an exit visa in Saudi Arabia? Discover the new rules for final exit, the Qiwa process, and mandatory requirements.

breadcrumb.name: Final Exit Visa Saudi Arabia: Processing Times & New Rules

contentHtml:
Navigating the departure from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) has become a digital-first process. With the continuous updates to the Labor Relation Initiative (LRI), both employers and employees must stay informed about the legal timelines and procedural shifts. Whether you are concluding a contract or managing a workforce, understanding the transition is vital for a compliant exit.

At Connect Resources, we simplify the complexities of Saudi Labor Law. This guide addresses the most frequent questions regarding the new rules in Saudi Arabia for final exit and exactly how many days to process an exit visa in Saudi Arabia.

1. How Many Days to Process an Exit Visa in Saudi Arabia?

The timeline for a final exit visa depends on the status of your documentation and the method of application.

  • Standard Processing (Via Absher/Muqeem): Once the request is submitted by the employer and all conditions (fines paid, no vehicles) are met, the visa is typically issued within 60 seconds to 24 hours electronically.

  • The 60-Day Validity Rule: After issuance, the individual has exactly 60 days to depart from the Kingdom. If you do not leave within this window, the visa must be cancelled and re-issued to avoid a fine of SAR 1,000.

  • Notice Period Consideration: While the visa issuance is fast, the legal “process” includes your notice period (usually 60 days for indefinite contracts), which must be served before the final exit is initiated on the Qiwa portal.

2. New Rules in Saudi Arabia for Final Exit

The Saudi Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD) has introduced several updates to balance the rights of both parties and increase labor market flexibility.

A. Digital Authentication via Qiwa

The most significant change is that the final exit process is now intrinsically linked to the Qiwa platform.

  • The employment contract must be digitally documented on Qiwa.

  • The system cross-references the contract end date with the exit request to ensure all notice periods are respected.

B. Exit During or After Contract Completion

Under the new rules in Saudi Arabia for final exit, an employee can initiate their own exit request via the “Labor Relation Movement” service if the contract has expired. If the contract is still active, the employer’s approval is required unless there is a breach of contract as per Article 81 of the Labor Law.

C. Automatic Cancellation of Residency (Iqama)

Upon the issuance of the final exit visa, the Iqama is technically cancelled, although it remains valid for domestic identification until the moment of departure at the airport.

3. Mandatory Requirements for a Smooth Exit

To avoid delays in your final exit visa, ensure the following criteria are met:

  1. Zero Traffic Fines: All violations registered on the Absher system must be paid.

  2. No Registered Vehicles: You cannot have any vehicle registered under your name (it must be sold or transferred).

  3. No Unpaid Loans: While the government doesn’t always block the visa for bank loans, banks can initiate a legal travel ban if they suspect a default.

  4. Valid Passport: Your passport must have at least 60 days of validity remaining.

4. Final Exit vs. Re-Entry: The Key Differences

Feature Final Exit Visa (Khurooj Nihai) Exit Re-Entry Visa
Purpose Permanent departure. Temporary travel with return.
Iqama Status Cancelled upon departure. Remains active.
Return to KSA Possible with a new work visa. Possible before visa expiry.
Validity Must leave within 60 days. Based on the duration requested.

5. End-of-Service Benefits (ESB) Calculation

Under the new rules in Saudi Arabia for final exit, the settlement of the End-of-Service Benefit is a mandatory step before the final departure.

  • Calculation: Half a month’s salary for each of the first five years, and a full month’s salary for each year thereafter.

  • Payment: The employer must settle this amount before the employee leaves to avoid potential labor disputes that could block the exit process.

6. How Connect Resources Can Help

Managing the exit of expatriate staff involves high-level coordination between HR, the Qiwa portal, and the Ministry of Interior. Connect Resources provides specialized PRO and EOR services to handle:

  • Final Settlement Audits: Ensuring all ESB and leave encashments are accurate.

  • Qiwa & Absher Management: Handling the digital submission and monitoring of exit visas.

  • Compliance Consulting: Mitigating the risk of “Huroob” (absconding) filings or labor disputes during the exit phase.

7. Conclusion: Planning Your Departure

The modern Saudi labor market is built on transparency. While the answer to how many days to process an exit visa in Saudi Arabia is “almost instantly” for the digital document itself, the administrative preparation—settling dues, serving notice, and closing bank accounts—should begin at least two months prior to your planned departure date.

FAQ: Final Exit in Saudi Arabia

Q1: Can I get a final exit if my Iqama is expired?

No. You must first renew the Iqama (and pay any associated fines) before a final exit visa can be issued.

Q2: Can an employer cancel a final exit visa after it’s issued?

Yes, but only within the 60-day validity period and through the Muqeem or Absher Business portal.

Q3: Does the final exit visa have a government fee?

The visa itself is free of charge, provided it is issued during the validity of a current Iqama.
